description:
In an interview with Al Jazeera, former Pentagon director for Arabian Peninsula Affairs David Des Roches said the priority in the Strait of Hormuz negotiations is restoring freedom of navigation for commercial shipping, arguing Iran is using its control over the waterway as leverage to deter future US attacks by creating "too high a price to pay". 
He described Iran's attacks on neutral civilian shipping as "a textbook definition of a war crime" and said charging ships to clear mines laid by Iran would amount to "a textbook definition of extortion". 
Des Roches argued the dispute is primarily a commercial rather than a military issue, with restoring confidence in global insurance markets essential for resuming normal trade. He warned that allowing Iran to impose transit fees would set a dangerous global precedent, potentially encouraging similar charges in other strategic waterways. Gaza has held its largest mass funeral for more than 100 members of two extended families killed in a single Israeli strike in 2023. Their remains are finally being laid to rest, giving surviving relatives a sense of closure after years of loss.

The funeral is taking place among the ruins of the Al-Sabra neighbourhood, which has been largely destroyed during Israel’s war on Gaza. The area was once home to the two families before the strike that killed them.

Al Jazeera’s Tareq Abu Azzoum reports live from Deir al-Balah.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
In an interview with Al Jazeera, Stephen Zunes, professor of politics at the University of San Francisco, argued Morocco helped facilitate the mass influx of migrants into Ceuta in what he described as a "setup" to increase pressure on Spain. 
He said Morocco has previously used migration as a form of "extortion" to secure political and economic concessions, while right-wing parties across Europe have exploited the crisis to fuel anti-immigrant sentiment. 
Zunes noted that Ceuta is outside continental Europe and the Schengen area, meaning the migrants have not entered mainland Spain. He also linked the crisis to Spain's foreign policy, citing Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's opposition to the US-Iran war—including refusing the use of US bases and banning overflights—and his support for Palestinian rights. 
Zunes said Morocco likely felt emboldened to allow the influx because it expected the United States and Israel to make political capital from the crisis.

description:
Fast-moving wildfires near Spokane have destroyed hundreds of homes and forced tens of thousands to evacuate, in what officials call one of Washington State's most destructive natural disasters. More than 900 firefighters are battling the blazes, which have been fuelled by dry conditions and strong winds. Governor Bob Ferguson has requested federal assistance as authorities warn the true scale of destruction remains unclear. The fires are part of a broader wildfire season across the western US, linked to hot, dry conditions driven by climate change.

Al Jazeera’s Manuel Rapalo reports from Washington, DC.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Iran has publicly confirmed that negotiations with Oman on the Strait of Hormuz are making progress, while firmly denying any direct engagement with the United States. Iran's foreign ministry announced that the talks are now focusing on creating a temporary route for vessels by merging both Iranian and Omani routes until a permanent agreement is reached. Regional mediators, including Qatar and Pakistan, remain active behind the scenes, suggesting diplomatic channels are still open despite the military posture. Meanwhile, US Central Command has announced its forces are fully prepared to protect commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, while the IRGC has said it is ready to retaliate to any threats. The creation of a single temporary route could be the first step towards building trust between Iran and the United States. 

Al Jazeera's Mahmoud Abdelwahed reports from Tehran.
